claim.aws-auto-scaling-faq-free-cloudwatch-fee: AWS Auto Scaling is free to use; because it is enabled by Amazon CloudWatch, service fees apply for CloudWatch and for your application resources, such as EC2 instances and Elastic Load Balancing load balancers.
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-change-instance-refresh: Since July 31, 2023, an instance refresh can be set to fail and optionally roll back when a chosen CloudWatch alarm goes into the ALARM state.
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-instance-refresh-min-ma: The minimum healthy percentage is the share of desired capacity kept in service, healthy and ready to use during an instance refresh; the maximum healthy percentage is the share of desired capacity that the group can increase to when it replaces instances.
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-max-instance-lifetime-m: The maximum instance lifetime must be at least 86,400 seconds (one day).
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-replace-root-volume-req: The replace root volume strategy requires a mixed instances policy whose overrides each specify an ImageId and AMIs that contain only a single root volume, and root volume replacement does not support Elastic Load Balancing.
claim.aws-auto-scaling-wa-free-managed-service: AWS Auto Scaling is a fully managed and free service to scale application capacity; it integrates with EC2 instances and Spot Fleets, Amazon ECS, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Aurora.
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-wa-replaces-unhealthy-i: Well-Architected auto-healing: when an instance is in any state other than running, or its system status is impaired, EC2 Auto Scaling considers the instance unhealthy and launches a replacement instance.
claim.ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pool-states: Warm pool instances can be kept in one of three states: Stopped, Running or Hibernated; keeping them Stopped is an effective way to minimize costs, because you pay only for the volumes and the attached Elastic IP addresses.
